receipt: S3-native HTF stamp convention — TWO-PATH resolution (R-068 §4)
why: Before the WIRE-1 structure wire may slice 4h/1h frames per-bar, the stamp convention must be KNOWN, not assumed. Under OPEN-stamping a naive `stamp <= t` filter admits the FORMING bar, whose OHLC contains bar-t future — the silent look-ahead R-067 §3 named, whose error direction is OPTIMISTIC.

path_1_from_code.conclusion: the repo's explicit in-engine resample is OPEN-stamped (label='left')
path_1_from_code.limitation: proves the in-engine WEEKLY resample only; says nothing about S3-native 4h/1h

path_2_empirical_alignment.method: Load MES 5min + S3-native 4h for 2022-03-01..2022-03-15. Convert both to UTC. Resample the 5m frame to 4h (closed='left', label='left') on the UTC grid. Join the S3-native 4h frame against the resampled bins under both stamping hypotheses and compare OHLC values.
path_2_empirical_alignment.conclusion: S3-native 4h bars are OPEN-STAMPED. The value match is EXACT (0.0000 on all four OHLC fields across all 67 overlapping bars) under H1 and grossly wrong under H2.

grid_anchor_finding.conclusion: the S3 4h grid is anchored to UTC 4h boundaries, NOT to ET midnight. A naive ET-anchored resample joins ZERO rows (verified) — an alignment bug that would have silently produced an empty or mis-stamped column.

different_instruments_check.question: R-068 §4 — if S3-native 4h cannot be made to match exec-resampled 4h at all (session filtering, roll handling), the two frames are different instruments and WHICH feeds structure is a fidelity decision.
different_instruments_check.finding: REFUTED — they match EXACTLY (0.0000 diff, 67/67 overlapping bars) once anchored to the UTC grid. Same instrument. No fidelity decision is forced.
different_instruments_check.residual: 67 S3 rows vs 68 resampled bins over the window: the resample produces one extra partial edge bin at the window boundary. Boundary effect, not a content disagreement.

TWO_PATH_VERDICT: AGREEMENT — code says OPEN-stamped, empirical alignment confirms OPEN-stamped. No alarm.

BINDING_RULE_for_the_structure_wire.rule: An HTF bar is available to exec bar t IFF its CLOSE time <= t (completed bars only).
BINDING_RULE_for_the_structure_wire.concretely_for_S3_4h: bars are OPEN-stamped, so close = stamp + 4h; therefore a 4h bar with stamp T is available to exec bar t IFF T + 4h <= t, i.e. T <= t - 4h.
BINDING_RULE_for_the_structure_wire.the_leak_this_prevents: a naive `T <= t` filter admits the bar stamped at or before t that has NOT closed — e.g. the bar stamped 08:00 covering 08:00-12:00 is NOT available at 10:30. Its high/low/close are computed from the bar-t FUTURE.
BINDING_RULE_for_the_structure_wire.still_owed: the intra-day STRADDLE case in the truncated-replay proof (an exec bar mid-way through a forming 4h bar) before the structure wire lands — R-067 §3.

one_hour_alignment_R069_s4.why: R-069 §4 made this BINDING: 'the 1h frame is NOT yet aligned — align it empirically before anything reads it.'
one_hour_alignment_R069_s4.method: identical to the 4h path — resample MES 5m→1h on the UTC grid, value-match against the S3-native 1h frame under both stamping hypotheses

row_counts.note: EXACT count match — no boundary or session-filter divergence at this window

one_hour_alignment_R069_s4.conclusion: S3-native 1h bars are OPEN-STAMPED, same as 4h. Binding rule: a 1h bar stamped T is available to exec bar t IFF T + 1h <= t.

scope: MES, 2022-03-01..2022-03-15. Both 4h and 1h now empirically aligned on ONE symbol and ONE window; the convention is a property of the S3 dataset layout, but a second symbol/window was not tested.
